A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Australian investors are more likely to support cross border acquisitions when the method of acquisition is stock and the target is located in a high investor protection country.
Australian bidders are able to create value in cross border acquisitions by acquiring private targets in foreign countries with strong investor protections and using the stock as a method of payment.
Australian acquirers' returns to cross border acquisitions are driven by a combination of target, acquirer and country specific factors, which are not necessarily related to the organisational form.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Australian investors perceive that cross border acquisitions create value for shareholders, and that the method of payment, the organisational form and the shareholder rights offered by the target firm matter for the returns to Australian acquirers.
the returns to Australian acquirers are driven by the characteristics of the target rather than the organisational form.
the organisational form and the method of payment are important in explaining the returns to Australian bidders in cross border acquisitions.
